title: The Spirit’s peace and joy in believers imply persuasion of divine favor
source_text: IX. Praeterea spiritus Christi in fidelium animis generat coelestem quandam pacem, & gaudium innarrabile. Nam ut docet Apostolus, Gal. 5. Fructus spiritus est charitas, gaudium, pax. Et Rom. 14. Regnum Dei est justitia & pax & gaudium in Spiritu Sancto. Quod gaudium & quam pacem experiri non potest, qui dubitat an sit Deo acceptus, & in ejus filiorum numero. Unde colligitur fideles qui tali gaudio & pace fruuntur, certo sibi persuadere posse se esse in Dei gratia. Neque enim quicquam delectare & exhilarare potest animum, nisi ex intimo & vivido sensu divini erga se amoris & favoris, & certa fiducia beatitudinis & gloriae aeternae.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, the Spirit of Christ generates in believers’ souls a certain heavenly peace and unspeakable joy. For as the Apostle teaches, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace (Gal. 5); and the kingdom of God is righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit (Rom. 14). That joy and that peace cannot be experienced by one who doubts whether he is accepted by God and numbered among his children. Hence it is gathered that believers who enjoy such joy and peace can certainly persuade themselves that they are in God’s grace. For nothing can delight and cheer the soul except from an inward and vivid sense of divine love and favor toward oneself, and a certain confidence of eternal blessedness and glory.
pass_b_english: Spirit-wrought peace and joy cannot sit with doubt that one is accepted by God.
Believers who taste that joy may rightly conclude they stand in grace.
